# extractor.sh agent documentation

> extractor.sh converts public URLs into reusable Markdown or normalized JSON through one cacheable HTTP GET endpoint.

Base URL: `https://extractor.mcb-software.workers.dev`

The public preview requires no account, API key, OAuth flow, or payment. Do not send credentials, cookies, private URLs, or non-public data.

## Hosted MCP server

Connect an MCP-compatible client to the stateless Streamable HTTP endpoint:

`https://extractor.mcb-software.workers.dev/mcp`

The server exposes one read-only tool, `extract_public_url`, with a required absolute public `url`, optional `format` of `markdown` (default) or `json`, and optional short `focus` topic. Use `focus` for requests such as pricing, features, or FAQ so the requested landing-page section is selected. Ordinary MCP and GET requests share extraction cache entries; focused MCP requests use topic-aware entries. All requests share rate limits. See `https://extractor.mcb-software.workers.dev/docs/mcp/` for configuration and usage.

## Endpoint

`GET /api/extract`

Query parameters:

- `url` — Required absolute public HTTP or HTTPS URL. Maximum length: 2048 characters.
- `format` — Optional. Use `json` (default) or `markdown`.

Example Markdown request:

```sh
curl --get 'https://extractor.mcb-software.workers.dev/api/extract' \
  --data-urlencode 'url=https://example.com/article' \
  --data-urlencode 'format=markdown'
```

Example JSON request:

```sh
curl --get 'https://extractor.mcb-software.workers.dev/api/extract' \
  --data-urlencode 'url=https://example.com/article' \
  --data-urlencode 'format=json'
```

## JSON response

Successful JSON responses contain:

- `schemaVersion` — Currently `1`.
- `type` — One of `document`, `article`, `product`, `post`, `profile`, `video`, `audio`, or `feed`.
- `source` — One of `web`, `amazon`, `app-store`, `bluesky`, `google-news`, `google-play`, `instagram`, `mastodon`, `reddit`, `shopify`, `soundcloud`, `spotify`, `tiktok`, `vimeo`, `x`, or `youtube`.
- `id` — Stable source identifier when available, otherwise `null`.
- `url` — Canonical source URL.
- `title` — Extracted title or `null`.
- `author` — Extracted author or `null`.
- `publishedAt` — ISO timestamp when available, otherwise `null`.
- `content` — Clean Markdown content.
- `media` — Public image, video, or audio references.
- `attributes` — Fields specific to the semantic entity type.
- `items` — Present for feed and profile responses; omitted for individual entities.

Each item follows the same entity shape. Product and variant `price` fields are non-negative integers in the currency's minor unit; for example, `1999` with `EUR` means €19.99. Use `priceDisplay` for presentation. Shared nullable fields are present with `null`, while unavailable optional attributes are omitted.

Software products can additionally include `softwareVersion`, `operatingSystem`, `contentRating`, and `developerUrl` attributes.

Machine-readable JSON Schema: `https://extractor.mcb-software.workers.dev/schemas/extraction-v1.json`

## Markdown response

With `format=markdown`, the response body is raw Markdown with `Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8`.

The public website pages also support HTTP content negotiation. Send `Accept: text/markdown` to any platform landing page to receive an agent-readable Markdown representation.

## Supported sources

### Web

Public HTTP and HTTPS articles, documentation, blogs, and other content pages. Submit the ordinary public page URL; extractor.sh handles supported pages automatically and returns a consistent response shape.

### Amazon

Public product detail pages from supported Amazon country stores return one product entity. Public search results URLs containing a `k` query return a feed with up to 20 product entities. Submit the ordinary product or search URL. Categories, pagination, carts, accounts, reviews, and personalized offers are not supported. Results may be cached for up to one hour.

Example: `https://www.amazon.de/product-name/dp/B09B8X9RGM`

Search example: `https://www.amazon.de/s?k=mechanical+keyboard`

### Apple App Store

Public Apple App Store app detail pages return one software product entity. Results can include the numeric app ID, name, developer, description, integer minor-unit price, ratings, version, operating-system requirement, release details, icon, and screenshots. Search, charts, reviews, accounts, and app downloads are not included. Results may be cached for up to one hour.

Example: `https://apps.apple.com/us/app/chatgpt/id6448311069`

### Bluesky

Public Bluesky profile pages return a profile entity with recent public post items. Exact public post pages return one post entity. Replies and parent threads are excluded. Profiles may omit complete embedded and quoted content.

Example: `https://bsky.app/profile/bsky.app`

Post example: `https://bsky.app/profile/bsky.app/post/3mqcp5qjdfs26`

### Google News

Public Google News search, topic, and top-stories pages return up to 50 article entities. Results can include public titles, publishers, dates, summaries, and source links. Full publisher article bodies, personalized For You results, Google Search, and Google Shopping are not included.

Example: `https://news.google.com/search?q=Cloudflare&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US%3Aen`

### Google Play

Public Google Play app detail pages return one software product entity. Results can include the Android package ID, name, developer, description, integer minor-unit price, rating, category, content rating, icon, and screenshots. Search, category browsing, reviews, accounts, and APK downloads are not included. Results may be cached for up to one hour.

Example: `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.openai.chatgpt`

### Instagram

Public Instagram post and reel pages return one post entity. Public profile pages return a profile entity with recent public post items. Private or login-only content, stories, comments, transcripts, and media downloads are unsupported.

Profile example: `https://www.instagram.com/instagram/`

### Mastodon

Public status pages on compatible instances return one post entity with text, author, date, content warning, and media descriptions when available. Private statuses, timelines, complete threads, and media downloads are unsupported.

Example: `https://mastodon.social/@trwnh/99664077509711321`

### Reddit

Public Reddit post pages, subreddit and community pages, and public user profile pages. Private and quarantined communities are unsupported. Post extraction does not include the complete comment tree.

Example: `https://www.reddit.com/r/CloudFlare/`

### Shopify

Public Shopify product pages return one product entity. Public storefront and collection pages return a feed with up to 50 product entities. Submit the ordinary public storefront page. Protected or unavailable storefront data may produce an incomplete result or an error.

Example: `https://store.example/products/black-shirt`

### SoundCloud

Public tracks, playlists, and sets return an audio entity; creator pages return a profile entity. Comments, waveforms, transcripts, and media downloads are not provided.

Example: `https://soundcloud.com/forss/flickermood`

### Spotify

Public tracks, albums, playlists, podcast shows, episodes, and supported short links return an audio entity; artist pages return a profile entity. Lyrics, transcripts, playback data, audio analysis, and media downloads are not provided.

Example: `https://open.spotify.com/episode/7makk4oTQel546B0PZlDM5`

### TikTok

Public TikTok video and photo post pages return one post entity. Public creator pages return a profile entity. Short links are supported when they resolve to one of these public pages. Private, deleted, or age-restricted content, comments, transcripts, and media downloads are unsupported.

Example: `https://www.tiktok.com/@scout2015/video/6718335390845095173`

### Vimeo

Public Vimeo video pages return one video entity with title, author, description, upload date, duration, thumbnail, and source URL when available. Transcripts, captions, comments, and media downloads are not provided.

Example: `https://vimeo.com/286898202`

### X

Public `x.com` and legacy `twitter.com` status URLs. Private, deleted, and age-gated posts are unsupported.

### YouTube

Public watch, Shorts, and `youtu.be` video pages, plus public channel, handle, legacy user, and playlist pages. Transcripts, captions, and media downloads are not provided.

Example: `https://www.youtube.com/@Cloudflare`

## Limits and caching

- General limit: 30 extraction requests per client per 60 seconds.
- High-cost extraction limit: 5 requests per client per 60 seconds.
- Product, profile, and feed results may be cached for 1 hour.
- Other single-entity results may be cached for 30 days.
- Maximum extracted result size: 2 MB.

Rate-limited responses use HTTP `429` and include `Retry-After` when available. Errors use a JSON object with `error.code` and `error.message`.

When a source blocks extraction or returns an upstream failure, the error message includes the upstream HTTP status when available. A `source_blocked` code means the source required authentication or denied access, commonly because of bot protection or access rules.

## Pricing

Pay-as-you-go billing is planned at €0.49 / 1,000 extractions. Credits never expire. Checkout is not yet available.
